title: Brick Breaker
description: Build a complete Brick Breaker game in Scratch 3. This self-guided course is for ages 10-14 with some Scratch experience. Across six chapters, you will control a paddle, move one Ball, create 50 bricks that each take two hits, drop Apple power-ups, track three lives, and end the game when every brick is gone.
objectives: Use coordinates, loops, conditions, variables, costumes, clones, and broadcasts in Scratch 3.
Build a reliable game loop in which miss detection happens before edge bouncing.
Make Ball the only sprite that checks for touching a brick, and use `broadcast Hit Brick and wait` so exactly one Brick clone reacts.
Create 50 bricks that always change from Healthy to Cracked before breaking.
Use Lives and Bricks Left to produce clear lose and win states that reset only with the green flag.
Test a multi-sprite project by checking one game rule at a time.
prerequisites: Know how to open Scratch 3 and start a new project.
Know how to drag blocks together and choose values from block menus.
Be able to rename sprites, costumes, backdrops, variables, and messages exactly as shown.
requirements: Use Scratch online at scratch.mit.edu, signed in to your Scratch account. You will not download or upload project files.
Complete all six chapters in order; there are no optional branches.
Create exactly four sprites named Paddle, Ball, Brick, and Apple.
Keep Ball as one original sprite and never create Ball clones.
Create exactly 50 Brick clones in five rows of ten.
Give every Brick clone the costumes Healthy and Cracked, in that order, so every brick requires two hits.
Start each Apple clone by going to Ball. Ball is still paused by `broadcast Hit Brick and wait`, so the Apple appears where the brick broke.
Create exactly three variables for all sprites named Lives, Bricks Left, and Hit Claimed, plus the Brick-only variable Is Clone.
Create exactly six messages named Build Bricks, Start Ball, Hit Brick, Apple Caught, Win, and Game Over.
Start every game with Lives set to 3, Bricks Left set to 50, and Hit Claimed set to 0.
Have only the Stage send Build Bricks and Start Ball at startup: wait for Build Bricks to finish before sending Start Ball.
Use Bricks Left, not score, to decide when the player wins.
Use the green flag as the only way to start or restart the game.

vocabulary.meaning: A number that describes a position. In Scratch, x moves left and right while y moves down and up.
A named place that stores a value the project can change and check.
A temporary copy of a sprite that uses the sprite's scripts but can move and act on its own.
A sprite that never makes copies of itself. Ball is one sprite with no clones, so "go to Ball" always means the same place.
An event that happens when two game objects touch.
A message that pauses the sender until every script started by that message has finished.
A shared variable that is 0 or 1. Ball sets it to 0 before a hit. The first Brick clone that reacts sets it to 1, so the other clones know the hit was already handled.
A script that reaches its last block because it has no `forever` loop. `broadcast and wait` can only continue after every script it started has finished.
A repeating script that updates movement, collisions, and game rules many times each second.
The current condition of an object or game, such as Healthy, Cracked, playing, won, or lost.

chapters.title: Project Foundations
objectives: Identify the complete game rules before coding.
Create and name all required project parts.
Control the Paddle with the mouse.

steps.title: Watch the Finished Game
steps.explanation: Brick Breaker is easier to build when you separate what you see from the rules underneath it. The player moves a Paddle. One Ball travels continuously. A grid contains 50 bricks. Every brick survives its first hit by changing from Healthy to Cracked, then disappears on its second hit. Missing the Paddle costs one of three lives. The game is won only when Bricks Left reaches 0.
instructions: Watch the example once without trying to copy code.
Watch again and look for the Paddle, the one Ball, five rows of ten bricks, and falling Apples.
Notice that a first brick hit changes its appearance and a second hit removes it.
Notice that a miss removes a life instead of bouncing from the bottom edge.
Remember that the green flag is the only start and restart control in the project.
hints: Count one row, then multiply ten bricks by five rows.
The video shows behavior; the exact code is built in the following steps.

debuggingTips.symptom: The final game seems like too many parts to remember.
checks: Say the four sprite names aloud: Paddle, Ball, Brick, Apple.
Write down the two ending rules: Lives equals 0 loses, and Bricks Left equals 0 wins.

checkpoint.task: Describe the required game path before opening the editor.
checkpoint.expectedResult: You can explain the two-hit brick rule, the three-life rule, and the win rule without guessing.
completeWhen: You know there will be exactly 50 bricks.
You know there is only one Ball and it never makes clones.
You know the green flag is the only restart.

steps.title: Create the Sprites, Backdrops, and Shared Data
steps.explanation: Exact names make later menus and code easy to follow. Lives and Bricks Left decide whether play continues. The shared Hit Claimed variable makes sure only one Brick clone reacts when Ball touches the bricks. Messages let the Stage run setup in order and let sprites work together.
instructions: Sign in to Scratch, click Create, and delete the Cat.
Type Brick Breaker in the project title box at the top of the editor.
Add or paint four sprites and name them exactly Paddle, Ball, Brick, and Apple.
Make Ball round and no wider than 20 pixels. Paint Paddle about 80 pixels wide and 10 pixels tall. Paint Brick about 40 pixels wide and 18 pixels tall.
Create three Stage backdrops named Play, You Win, and Game Over. Keep the ending backdrops simple and readable.
Make three variables for all sprites named Lives, Bricks Left, and Hit Claimed.
Create six messages named Build Bricks, Start Ball, Hit Brick, Apple Caught, Win, and Game Over.
Do not make a Restart sprite, Restart message, restart key, or Ball clone.
hints: Use the paint editor if a library sprite is too large or detailed.
Variable and message names must include the spaces shown here.
Keep Ball no wider than 20 pixels. A bigger Ball touches the bottom edge and bounces before the miss check can see it.

debuggingTips.symptom: A sprite or variable does not appear in a block menu.
checks: Check its spelling and capitalization.
Confirm Lives, Bricks Left, and Hit Claimed were made for all sprites, not for one sprite only.

checkpoint.task: Check the sprite list, backdrop list, Variables category, and message menus.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The project contains only the four required sprites, three named backdrops, three shared variables, and six named messages.
completeWhen: All sprite, backdrop, variable, and message names match the instructions exactly.
There is no restart control.
Ball has no clones or clone-making script.

steps.title: Set Up the Game and Control the Paddle
steps.explanation: The Stage sets the starting values because they belong to the whole game. It resets all three shared variables, tells Brick to build the grid, waits for that to finish, and only then tells Ball to start. Paddle follows only mouse x, so it moves sideways but stays at the same height near the bottom.
instructions: On the Stage, add a green-flag script that switches to Play, sets Lives to 3, sets Bricks Left to 50, and sets Hit Claimed to 0.
Next, broadcast Build Bricks and wait. After that block, broadcast Start Ball without adding a wait.
On Paddle, add a green-flag script that shows Paddle and sets its size to 100 percent.
Next, go to x 0, y -145. Then add a forever loop that sets x to mouse x.
Drag the mouse left and right while the project runs.
Keep Paddle's y fixed. Do not use a forever block to change y.
hints: The `mouse x` block is in Sensing.
Using `set x to (mouse x)` makes movement direct and beginner-friendly.

debuggingTips.symptom: Paddle moves once and then stops.
checks: Put `set x to (mouse x)` inside `forever`.
Make sure the script begins with `when green flag clicked`.

debuggingTips.symptom: Paddle moves up and down.
checks: Use mouse x, not mouse y.
Use `go to x: (0) y: (-145)` only before the forever loop.

checkpoint.task: Start the project and move the mouse across the Stage.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The Play backdrop appears, Lives shows 3, Bricks Left shows 50, Hit Claimed starts at 0, and Paddle follows left and right at the same height.
completeWhen: Paddle starts centered at y -145.
Paddle follows mouse x continuously.
Clicking the green flag restores Paddle size to 100.

finishedCode.code:
when green flag clicked
switch backdrop to [Play v]
set [Lives v] to (3)
set [Bricks Left v] to (50)
set [Hit Claimed v] to (0)
broadcast [Build Bricks v] and wait
broadcast [Start Ball v]

when green flag clicked
show
set size to (100) %
go to x: (0) y: (-145)
forever
  set x to (mouse x)
end

instructions: Stop the project. Drag Paddle to one side and type 150 into the size box in the sprite info below the Stage.
In the Variables category, choose Lives in the `set to` block, type 9, and click the block. Lives now shows 9. Do the same for Bricks Left and Hit Claimed.
Click the green flag once.
Confirm the backdrop, variables, Paddle position, and Paddle size all reset.
Compare your scripts with the complete code so far, shown below, before continuing.
Choose File > Save now.
hints: Later, the green flag will also remove old clones. That is another reason it is the only way to restart.

chapters.title: Ball Movement and Lives
objectives: Keep Ball as one original sprite.
Order miss detection before edge bouncing.
Reset Ball after a miss and lose after three misses.
Bounce Ball upward from Paddle.

steps.title: Prepare One Ball
steps.explanation: Ball is one sprite and never makes clones. Its main script starts only when it receives Start Ball. The Stage sends that message after Build Bricks has finished, so Ball never needs a guessed wait.
instructions: Select Ball and remove any clone blocks if you experimented with them.
Keep Ball no wider than 20 pixels. If you chose the library Ball, a size of about 25-35 percent works.
Add a short green-flag script that hides Ball while the Stage builds the bricks.
Begin Ball's main script with `when I receive Start Ball`, then set rotation style to all around.
Go to x 0 y -100, point in a random direction from -45 to 45, and show.
Do not add a second Ball sprite or any `create clone of Ball` block.
hints: In Scratch, direction 0 points up. Directions from -45 to 45 launch Ball upward.
Build Bricks and wait keeps Ball hidden until the complete grid is ready.

debuggingTips.symptom: Ball launches downward.
checks: Use `pick random (-45) to (45)`.
Do not use 135 to 225, which points downward.

checkpoint.task: Click the green flag several times. Each time, look at Ball and at the direction in its sprite info.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Exactly one Ball appears at x 0, y -100 after Start Ball. Its direction is a different number from -45 to 45 each time.
completeWhen: Ball is hidden until Start Ball is received.
Ball always begins from the same position.
No script creates a Ball clone.

finishedCode.code:
when green flag clicked
hide

when I receive [Start Ball v]
set rotation style [all around v]
go to x: (0) y: (-100)
point in direction (pick random (-45) to (45))
show

steps.title: Move, Detect a Miss, Then Bounce
steps.explanation: The order of these checks is a game rule. Each loop pass first moves Ball. Next it checks whether Ball fell below y -165. Only after that check does `if on edge, bounce` run. If the edge bounce came first, the bottom edge could send Ball back up and the player would never lose a life.
instructions: After `show` in the Start Ball script, add a forever loop and move 8 steps.
Immediately after moving, check whether y position is less than -165.
On a miss, change Lives by -1.
If Lives equals 0, broadcast Game Over and wait, then stop all.
Otherwise, hide Ball and go to x 0, y -100.
Then point in a random direction from -45 to 45, wait 1 second, and show.
Place `if on edge, bounce` after the complete miss condition, never before it.
hints: Use an `if then else` inside the miss condition to separate the last life from a normal reset.
The 1-second pause gives the player time to move Paddle under the new launch.

debuggingTips.symptom: Ball bounces from the bottom and Lives does not change.
checks: Move the y-position miss condition above `if on edge, bounce`.
Check that the miss value is -165, not 165.

debuggingTips.symptom: Lives keeps falling rapidly after one miss.
checks: Reset Ball to y -100 inside the else branch.
Make sure the reset happens before the loop repeats.

checkpoint.task: Move Paddle away and let Ball miss once.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Lives changes from 3 to 2, Ball pauses at its reset position, and then launches upward again.
completeWhen: One miss removes exactly one life.
The bottom edge never bounces Ball back into play.
The miss check appears before edge bounce in the script.

finishedCode.code:
when green flag clicked
hide

when I receive [Start Ball v]
set rotation style [all around v]
go to x: (0) y: (-100)
point in direction (pick random (-45) to (45))
show
forever
  move (8) steps
  if <(y position) < (-165)> then
    change [Lives v] by (-1)
    if <(Lives) = (0)> then
      broadcast [Game Over v] and wait
      stop [all v]
    else
      hide
      go to x: (0) y: (-100)
      point in direction (pick random (-45) to (45))
      wait (1) seconds
      show
    end
  end
  if on edge, bounce
end

steps.title: Return Ball from Paddle
steps.explanation: Touching Paddle should always send Ball upward. Moving Ball forward immediately after changing direction separates the sprites, preventing repeated collision checks while they overlap.
instructions: In Ball's forever loop, add a Paddle-touch condition after `if on edge, bounce`.
When touching Paddle, point in a random direction from -60 to 60.
Move 12 steps immediately so Ball leaves Paddle before the next loop.
Test catches near the left edge, center, and right edge of Paddle.
Keep this collision in Ball. Paddle should not contain a Ball-touch loop.
hints: A wider random range creates more varied shots while still pointing upward.
If Ball is wider than 20 pixels, shrink it instead of increasing the separation move.

debuggingTips.symptom: Ball shakes or changes direction many times on Paddle.
checks: Put `move (12) steps` inside the touching-Paddle condition.
Make sure the random directions are -60 to 60.

debuggingTips.symptom: Ball passes through Paddle.
checks: Confirm the sensing menu says Paddle.
Reduce Ball speed from 8 if your Paddle costume is extremely thin.

checkpoint.task: Keep Ball in play for at least five Paddle bounces.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Each Paddle touch sends Ball upward once at a varied angle without sticking.
completeWhen: Paddle catches work across its width.
Ball separates after each catch.
Paddle has no collision script.

chapters.title: Fifty Two-Hit Bricks
objectives: Create a five-by-ten clone grid.
Represent brick health with Healthy and Cracked costumes.
Make Ball the only sprite that checks for touching a brick.
Use Hit Claimed so exactly one clone reacts to each hit, in a Hit Brick script that finishes.

steps.title: Paint Healthy and Cracked, Then Build the Grid
steps.explanation: The hidden original Brick creates all 50 clones when it receives Build Bricks. A repeat inside a repeat makes ten clones across each row and five rows down. The `For this sprite only` variable Is Clone is 1 in clones and 0 in the original. Each clone starts in the Healthy costume, so no brick starts damaged.
instructions: In Brick's Costumes tab, name the first costume Healthy.
Duplicate it, draw obvious crack lines without changing its outer size, and name the copy Cracked.
On Brick, make a variable named Is Clone for this sprite only.
Add a green-flag script on Brick that hides the original.
Add `when I receive Build Bricks`. Hide the original and set Is Clone to 0.
Then switch to Healthy and go to x -216, y 150.
Use an outer repeat 5 and inner repeat 10. Create a clone, then change x by 48 inside the inner repeat.
After each row, set x to -216 and change y by -30.
After all rows, move the hidden original to x 240, y 180.
Then add `wait 0 seconds`. This short pause lets every clone run its start script before Build Bricks finishes.
Under `when I start as a clone`, set Is Clone to 1, switch to Healthy, and show.
hints: Ten positions from -216 through 216 fit across the Stage.
The original moves away so it cannot be confused with a clone during sensing.

debuggingTips.symptom: There are 45, 55, or another wrong number of bricks.
checks: Set the outer repeat to 5 and inner repeat to 10.
Keep `create clone of myself` inside both repeats.

debuggingTips.symptom: Rows form a diagonal instead of a grid.
checks: After the inner repeat, set x back to -216.
Change y by -30 only once per completed row.

checkpoint.task: Click the green flag and count the grid by rows and columns after Build Bricks finishes.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Exactly 50 visible Healthy clones appear as five rows of ten before Ball starts, while the original Brick remains hidden.
completeWhen: Every row has ten clones.
There are five rows.
Every visible brick uses Healthy before Start Ball is sent.

when green flag clicked
hide

when I receive [Build Bricks v]
hide
set [Is Clone v] to (0)
switch costume to [Healthy v]
go to x: (-216) y: (150)
repeat (5)
  repeat (10)
    create clone of [myself v]
    change x by (48)
  end
  set x to (-216)
  change y by (-30)
end
go to x: (240) y: (180)
wait (0) seconds

when I start as a clone
set [Is Clone v] to (1)
switch costume to [Healthy v]
show

steps.title: Let Ball Check for Brick Hits
steps.explanation: Only Ball checks whether it is touching Brick. On a touch, Ball sets Hit Claimed to 0, then sends Hit Brick with `broadcast and wait`. In the next step, the first touching clone will set Hit Claimed to 1, so the clones next to it do nothing. While Ball waits, it stays paused at the brick. Then Ball checks for a win, turns around, and moves away from the brick.
instructions: In Ball's forever loop, add a touching-Brick condition after the Paddle condition.
Inside it, set Hit Claimed to 0, then use `broadcast Hit Brick and wait`, not ordinary broadcast.
After the message returns, check whether Bricks Left equals 0. If so, broadcast Win and wait, then stop all.
If play continues, point in direction `direction + 180 + pick random -20 to 20` and move 12 steps to separate from the brick.
Do not put the broadcast in its own forever script. Only broadcast when Ball is touching Brick.
hints: The `direction` block is in Motion. Put it in the `+` block. Scratch keeps the result between -180 and 180.
The receiver built next must end quickly so broadcast-and-wait can return.
The small random turn changes Ball's path after each brick, so it does not fly straight back to the same spot on Paddle.

debuggingTips.symptom: Ball freezes forever on its first brick touch.
checks: Look for a `when I receive Hit Brick` script containing `forever`; remove that loop.
Make sure every Hit Brick script reaches its last block.

debuggingTips.symptom: Ball travels through bricks without requesting a hit.
checks: Put the touching-Brick condition inside Ball's main forever loop.
Select Brick in the touching block's menu.

checkpoint.task: Click the green flag, keep Ball in play, and watch it reach the bricks.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Ball turns back each time it touches a brick. No brick cracks yet, because Brick does not answer Hit Brick until the next step.
completeWhen: Ball contains the only touching-Brick sensing block.
Hit Claimed is set to 0 immediately before broadcast and wait.
The win check uses Bricks Left.

steps.title: Damage Every Brick Twice
steps.explanation: The original Brick and every clone receive Hit Brick. Only a clone that is touching Ball while Hit Claimed is 0 reacts. That clone sets Hit Claimed to 1 first, before changing costume or deleting itself, so no other clone reacts to the same hit. Healthy changes to Cracked on the first hit. A Cracked clone lowers Bricks Left and deletes itself on the second hit. The script has no loop, so it finishes and Ball's `broadcast and wait` can continue.
instructions: On Brick, add `when I receive Hit Brick` as a separate script.
Add an `if` block. Put an `and` block in its condition, then put a second `and` block in the left side of the first one.
Fill the three spaces with `Is Clone = 1`, `touching Ball?`, and `Hit Claimed = 0`. The clone does nothing unless all three are true.
As the first block inside the condition, set Hit Claimed to 1. Then compare costume name with Healthy.
If the costume name is Healthy, switch costume to Cracked.
Otherwise, change Bricks Left by -1 and delete this clone.
Do not add forever, repeat, wait, or a Ball-touch script under `when I start as a clone`.
hints: Use the `costume name` block from Looks, not costume number.
Deleting a clone stops its script, so change Bricks Left before deletion.

debuggingTips.symptom: A Healthy brick disappears on the first hit.
checks: Check that the then branch switches to Cracked.
Put Bricks Left change and deletion only in the else branch.

debuggingTips.symptom: Bricks Left decreases on the first hit.
checks: Move `change Bricks Left by -1` into the else branch.
Confirm each clone starts with Healthy.

checkpoint.task: Watch one brick through two separate Ball contacts.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The first contact changes Healthy to Cracked without changing Bricks Left; the second removes it and changes 50 to 49.
completeWhen: No brick breaks while Healthy.
Every broken brick subtracts exactly one.
Exactly one touching clone changes on each contact.
The Hit Brick receiver contains no loop.

finishedCode.code:
when I receive [Hit Brick v]
if <<<(Is Clone) = (1)> and <touching [Ball v]?>> and <(Hit Claimed) = (0)>> then
  set [Hit Claimed v] to (1)
  if <(costume [name v]) = [Healthy]> then
    switch costume to [Cracked v]
  else
    change [Bricks Left v] by (-1)
    delete this clone
  end
end

steps.explanation: Ball and Brick now work together. Ball is the only sprite that checks for touching a brick and decides when to wait. Each Brick clone only changes its costume or deletes itself. Bricks Left counts the bricks still on the Stage, not hits or points.
instructions: Click the green flag and confirm Stage finishes Build Bricks before it sends Start Ball.
Observe at least three first hits and three second hits.
Confirm one clone responds per contact, first hits never change Bricks Left, and second hits always reduce it by one.
Check that no Brick script has a forever loop around its hit code.
Compare Ball and Brick with the complete code so far.
Choose File > Save now.
hints: Use the stop button after testing if you do not want to finish the whole game yet.

debuggingTips.symptom: Several hits happen during one overlap.
checks: Confirm Ball sets Hit Claimed to 0 immediately before broadcast-and-wait.
Confirm the touching Brick clone sets Hit Claimed to 1 before changing costume or deleting itself.
Confirm Ball moves 12 steps after broadcast-and-wait.
Confirm Brick has no forever loop that checks for touching Ball.

steps.title: Trace One Frame of Collision Work
steps.explanation: Games often break when two scripts react to the same touch. In this project, each touch has one job: Ball checks for Paddle and Brick, Hit Claimed lets one touching Brick clone react, Apple checks for Paddle to see if it was caught, and Paddle only reacts to Apple Caught.
instructions: Check that Ball has one forever loop for movement and collision checks.
Check that Ball sets Hit Claimed to 0 right before `broadcast Hit Brick and wait`.
Check that Brick's Hit Brick script needs Is Clone = 1, touching Ball, and Hit Claimed = 0, and then sets Hit Claimed to 1 first.
Check that Paddle never checks touching Ball or Brick.
Check that only Apple clones check touching Paddle.
Run contacts near the border between two bricks and watch exactly one clone change costume or delete.
Confirm Ball points in direction `direction + 180 + pick random -20 to 20` and moves 12 steps after each hit response.
hints: A script with `if` blocks still finishes. Only a `forever` loop, or a repeat that never ends, keeps it from finishing.

The turn of about 180 degrees and the 12-step move send Ball back out the way it came in, so it leaves the brick from any impact direction. The random part is at most 20 degrees, so the move still clears the brick.
